title: LEGO Scout deal record
description: The canonical shape of one `deals[]` row. Full field semantics live in references/output_contract.md; this file exists to let a phase's field set be QUERIED (`phase == "crawl"` etc.) instead of hand-maintained as a second document. `crawl` fields come from legoscout-sources (the listing page itself). `appraisal` fields come from legoscout-pricing plus the vision pass. `synthesis` fields are written only by legoscout-ledger/scripts/build_deal_record.py, which assembles the other two into one record -- including every mirror column.

source.description: The listing_key namespace; must match source_names.CANONICAL for the namespace. The display name is derived at render time and never stored.

title.description: Listing title, or `unknown` only after direct-page verification.

direct_url.description: Direct listing URL used by callers; same as `url` unless a canonical URL differs.

auction_start_date.description: When bidding opens, or `not-an-auction`/`unknown`. The value is an ISO date or one of the two sentinels VERBATIM; an explanation belongs in `notes`, not here.

bidding_open.description: Whether the lot accepts a bid RIGHT NOW, as the worker observed it. Prefer `auction_start_date`: a date self-updates against the clock, a flag goes stale. Set this when the source publishes no bid-open timestamp but the lot is visibly live -- AuctionZip, AuctionNinja, K-BID and eBay all publish none, and eBay dropped 2 good lots on 2026-08-04 because the contract demanded a date that does not exist. `null` on a fixed-price row and whenever openness was not read.

auction_end_date.description: When bidding closes, or `not-an-auction`/`unknown`. The value is an ISO date or one of the two sentinels VERBATIM; an explanation belongs in `notes`, not here.

current_price.description: Current auction/listing price. `0` is valid on a zero-bid auction.

buy_now_price.description: Buy It Now/static price when available.

price_basis.description: Which price field is authoritative; see the source module's `PRICE_BASIS_RULE`. Every value here must be a key of `schema.PRICE_BASIS_COLUMNS`. A fixed ask is `static_price`: the retired `ask_price` named one column while its rows filled another, so 256 of 484 rows carried no readable price at all. The retired `estimated` named no column, so a $45 listing could store a $999 hammer and pass `--strict`.

weight_lbs.description: Weight in pounds AS STATED on the listing. A vision-estimated weight lives at `observations.vision.weight_estimate_lbs`, not here. BOUNDED, because nothing else bounds it: not the scorer, not build_deal_record, not validate. `weight_lbs: 1e300` on a $45.00 bulk lot scored 97 with `max_price` 4.88e+300 and `--strict` reported no error, because $/lb is landed/weight and a big enough divisor makes any price look free. 2000 lb is a full shipping pallet of loose LEGO -- the physical ceiling on a lot one person collects or has freighted. The heaviest weight the ledger has ever stored is 100 lb. The floor is 0.01 lb -- one 4.5 g minifigure, the smallest LEGO object that can be a lot -- because `weight_lbs: 1e-9` is the same defect pointed the other way: it drove $/lb to 5.5e+10 and `max_price` to $0.00, which is a listing deleted from the table rather than promoted to the top of it. Exactly 0 is allowed ALONGSIDE that floor, not instead of it, because nine rows already store it (three of them active) as ShopGoodwill's 'no weight published'; that is what `null` is for, those rows want repairing, and rejecting them here would make the whole ledger unwritable.

item_location.description: Listing's stated location, verbatim and state-qualified.

origin_zip.description: Seller's ship-FROM ZIP, when the listing exposes one.

seller_id.description: The marketplace's own stable seller key, verbatim as a string (ShopGoodwill `sellerId`, Poshmark `lister_id`, OfferUp `ownerId`, an eBay username). `null` carries two meanings, told apart by that source's reader module: a module that writes no `seller_id()` and says why in `NEEDS_PAGE_READ` (Craigslist, StockX) means the marketplace has no seller identity, and a module that does read one means the worker did not and said so in `evidence_summary`. Never invent one.

seller_name.description: The seller's display name, store name, or auction house, verbatim. Same `null` rule as `seller_id`. ShopGoodwill sellers 8, 43, 122 and 376 produce consistently different landed $/lb; this field is what makes that queryable instead of prose in a source note.

available_fulfillment.description: Non-empty subset of `["local_pickup", "shipping"]`, read off the listing per that source's `available_fulfillment()` reader.

image_urls.description: Listing photo URLs, captured through the source's authenticated CLI.

shipping_estimate.description: The SOURCE's own destination-rate quote to 47725, or an explicit unquoted answer with a reason. `null` means the source publishes no rate at all (HiBid, K-BID, Facebook). Written only through `shipping_estimate.py`'s quoted()/unquoted(); `total_of()` computes the delivered charge. `destination_zip`, `country` and `total` are NOT stored: the first two are project constants and the third is derived from its own parts, and storing a derived value is what let one number disagree with itself.

handling_price.description: null means the source publishes no separate handling line, the normal Poshmark/eBay/Depop shape

reason.description: why no rate exists -- pickup only, weight invalid, freight invoiced after the sale

winning_bid.description: Closed-auction hammer price, when the source reports one.

price_override.description: Evidence-backed correction of a crawl price the listing's own text contradicts. `price` is the seller's actual ask parsed from that text and `evidence` quotes it verbatim; both REQUIRED when the object is present, null when absent. Fixed-price asks only -- an auction hammer belongs to bidding, never to description prose. Applied deterministically by build_deal_record (_apply_price_override): static_price, price_basis and fee_breakdown.hammer move to the override before any landed cost or score is computed. Born 2026-08-24 from facebook|1024732190360342, where a $5 placeholder hid five sets priced $200 in the body yet scored 100 off the phantom $5.

listing_category.description: `bulk` (multi-pound loose LEGO lot), `set` (one or more complete sets, used or new), `minifigure` (a single minifigure or a lot of minifigures), or `excluded` (not a LEGO-piece listing at all: books, hardware/storage, displays, manuals only, or anything the classifier excluded -- always recorded as `status: rejected`, never active).

exclusion_reason.description: Why the classifier excluded this listing (books/hardware/non-brick item, partial set with no complete-set identity, etc.). Required non-empty whenever `listing_category` is `excluded`; null otherwise. Displayed in `notes` on the rejected record.

figure_count.description: How many minifigures the listing contains. Stated count from the listing text first; otherwise an exact count read off the listing photos -- inspecting the images is MANDATORY for every minifigure candidate, so a null means text and photos both failed to yield a countable answer, never a skipped look. On identifier-backed rows (`figure_count_source`=`detection`) synthesis OWNS this value: build_record derives it from `minifig_analysis`, and classifier stated/photo counts survive only under `observations.vision` as mismatch evidence. Provenance is `figure_count_source`.

figure_count_source.description: How `figure_count` was determined on a minifigure lot: `stated` (the seller's own text), `photo_count` (counted off the listing images by the mandatory vision pass), `unknown` (images were inspected but no exact count was determinable), or `detection` (the identifier pipeline owns the count; required on every new identifier-backed row, where the value equals the sum of `minifig_analysis` entry quantities). Null on every non-minifigure category. Required whenever `figure_count` is a number.

set_completeness.description: `complete`, `incomplete`, or `unknown` — decided by the Completeness Gate before any BrickLink pricing.

potential_profit.description: Net-of-fees resale less landed cost, set-category only.

profit_incomplete.description: True when any detected set could not be priced, or completeness is not `complete`.

ebay_avg_sold_price.description: eBay sold-listing average price from `legoscout pricing comps`/`ebay-comps`, set category only. On a SET record this lot-level SUM stays informational, same as `used_avg_6mo`/`new_avg_6mo` (BrickLink) -- the actual profit input is the per-set `set_analysis[].blended_avg_sold_price`, a comp-count-weighted average of BrickLink's selected-condition sold price and this same eBay number, computed by `legoscout_cli.ledger.build_record._apply_comps` (see `set_analysis[].comp_basis` for the derivation). On a BULK record this field is still never fed into `potential_profit` or the score -- bulk has no BrickLink comp to blend against.

ebay_comp_count.description: How many eBay sold listings backed `ebay_avg_sold_price` after exact set-number-token matching and denylist exclusion.

ebay_avg_price_per_lb.description: eBay sold $/lb average for a bulk lot, from `legoscout pricing comps --bulk`. Informational for bulk; not fed into `potential_profit`.

ebay_avg_price_per_fig.description: LEGACY evidence from the retired eBay $/fig pricing path, kept readable on rows classified before per-figure identification. Current code never writes it: new minifigure rows price through `minifig_analysis` per-figure BrickLink used-sold values instead. Deliberately NOT in RETIRED_COLUMNS -- connect-time retirement would destroy this preserved evidence.

shipping_estimated.description: True when `shipping_estimate`/`fee_breakdown.shipping_handling` was computed rather than quoted by the source.

confidence.description: `high`, `medium`, `low`, or `unknown` — capped at `medium` for a purely visual set ID.

destination_zip_note.description: Note on how the destination ZIP 47725 was applied, when relevant.

pickup_miles.description: Road-miles proxy from ZIP 47725, via `legoscout-pricing/scripts/pickup_area.py`. `null` when outside the 30-mile pickup set.

zero_comp_note.description: Why a six-month sold average is missing, in the appraiser's own words: `no sold comps`, `no set # in listing`, `set # not in BrickLink`, or `used avg unavailable: unpriced` when only one condition is missing. `unknown` when nothing is missing. This is the ONLY home for that reason -- 51 rows kept it inside `used_avg_6mo`/`new_avg_6mo`, which are typed `number|null` and which no profit calculation could then read. `build_rows.mjs`'s `compValue` renders it in the comp cell and `serve_deals.py` renders it as the dagger tooltip.

fee_breakdown.description: Hammer, premium, tax, and shipping/handling breakdown. `hammer` must equal the price named by `price_basis`, and is REQUIRED: `build_deal_record._resolve_shipping` rebuilds the landed total around it whenever the source quotes freight, and a missing one used to be read as a $0.00 item. TYPED, with the same rigor `shipping_estimate` carries. It was a bare `object` with no `properties` for its whole life, so an appraiser writing `premium_pct: "18%"` cleared build_deal_record AND `deals validate --strict` (`{"checked": 4, "invalid": 0}`) and then threw in legoscout_cli/display/rows.py with `unsupported format character '%'` -- which returns ZERO rows for the WHOLE ledger, so three clean deals were lost alongside the one poisoned row. `validate.py` already argues an illegal `listing_type` is an ERROR precisely because the page throws on anything else; this field had the identical consequence and no rule at all. Every numeric line is bounded as well as typed: `inf` and `NaN` are floats that pass a bare `number`, and a `maximum` is what rejects `inf` (`NaN` is caught separately by `schema._reject_non_finite`, since it fails no comparison). `additionalProperties: false` is what stops the NEXT invented spelling; the block below the canonical keys is the 26 that already reached the ledger before anything enforced one shape, kept only so the stored rows stay writable. They are LEGACY: nothing reads them, `fees.landed_cost` writes none of them, and a producer emitting one today is writing a fee nothing will price. Fold them into the canonical keys and delete them from here.

premium_pct.description: Buyer premium as a FRACTION (0.18), never a percent (18) and never a string ('18%'). rows.py renders it with `%.1f%%` and throws on anything that is not a number.

buyer_protection_fee.description: The numeric buyer fee published by the marketplace. Mercari calls this the Buyer Protection fee and exposes it in priceSummary.

sales_tax_pct.description: Sales tax as a FRACTION (0.07), same rule as premium_pct.

shipping_handling.description: Freight plus handling, and the ONLY freight figure the deals page reads. `null` DECLARES it unknown, which is different from free.

fee_multiple.description: `landed_total / hammer`. `null` on a $0.00 hammer, where the ratio does not exist.

set_numbers.description: Detected BrickLink set numbers, set-category only.

set_analysis.description: One entry per detected set: BrickLink catalog metadata plus 6-month sold summaries, from `lookup_set_sales.py`. An ARRAY because `summarize_set()` returns exactly one per-set object and the appraiser calls it once per set; `null` when no set was priced, and never `[]`, which is the same answer spelled twice. It was typed `object|null` until 2026-08-05 while 331 rows already held the array, and the ledger carried four incompatible dict spellings beside it (a `sets` wrapper, keyed by set number, a bare per-set object, an unkeyed blob). Read and write it only through `legoscout-ledger/scripts/set_analysis.py` -- `normalize()`/`entries()`/`names()`. A lot-level value (`potential_profit_total`, `purchase_price`, `used_avg_6mo`, `set_numbers`) does NOT belong in an entry: it has its own column, and the wrapper copy had already gone stale on 7 rows.

minifig_analysis.description: One entry per identifier match group behind a minifigure row: stable-ref detections, Brickognize candidates, agent verification, verified identity (fig_no + catalog), detector-owned quantity, condition notes, and per-figure BrickLink used-sold value. Written by `legoscout minifig price`; null on every legacy row. Read/write ONLY through legoscout_cli/ledger/minifig_analysis.py -- normalize()/entries()/entry_errors(); that module solely owns entry semantics, this schema gates only array-or-null shape. Cross-photo repeats collapse into one entry's quantity (max simultaneous in any photo); unknown/unverifiable figures stay present with crops and null values, never estimates.

first_seen_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when first recorded. Preserved across updates, never recomputed.

last_seen_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when last verified or updated.

model_score.description: Mirror of `scoring.model_score`, the model's advisory verdict.

last_price.description: Display-only human-readable price summary, derived from the numeric price fields — never the sole record of the price.

notes.description: Evidence-backed rationale, risk note, or update note.

prospect_id.description: Link to the prospect that produced this deal. NULL until phase 2.

observations.description: `text_signals.scan()` output merged with the appraiser's `vision`/`description`/`model_score`, via `score_deal.build_observations()`. Only ONE key inside it is typed here, and deliberately so: `vision.weight_estimate_lbs` is the model-authored twin of `weight_lbs` and feeds the same $/lb divisor, so it carries the same bound. The rest of this object is `text_signals.scan()` output owned by legoscout_cli/scoring, and typing it from here would be a second, drifting copy of a contract that module already owns -- it belongs in scoring, next to the code that writes it. `additionalProperties` stays open for the same reason.

weight_estimate_lbs.description: Vision-estimated weight in pounds. Same bound as `weight_lbs`, because the scorer falls back to this divisor when the listing states no weight, and an absurd value here inflates the score exactly the same way.

scoring.description: Output of `score_deal.score_record()`. The only place a scoring number may be written.

verification.description: Legacy verification metadata; not part of the documented output contract.
